children: DAT said U.S. truckload spot linehaul rates saw the steepest July–August drops in its 16-year history, with van and reefer spot rates falling back below contract levels. Diesel surcharges also rose in August, adding carrier cost pressure.
Signals sharp softening in dry van demand/pricing vs July.
Cold-chain pricing slid; spot fell back below contracts.
Spot-contract gap reopened, favoring shippers over carriers.
Fuel costs rose even as spot rates fell, squeezing carriers.
Confirms softer demand alongside pricing declines.

This is a mid-cycle confirmation of softer truckload spot pricing after a brief summer uptick that pushed spot above contracts. A sustained demand rebound or capacity exits causing tightening would be needed to flip spot above contract and become a stronger catalyst.
